rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (base_speed 1.0, kd 0.30, kp 4.0, ki 0.05, search_left, sensors at ±0.05 m, sensor_size 0.016) is the best raced design at 85.60. Its oval progress is 0.3425 with 0 line-loss events, but oval max_error is 0.0623, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit. S-bend and slalom each lose the line once per run (progress 0.1625 and 0.110). Those two tracks have now shown one loss per run under last_direction, search_right, and search_left, at speeds from 1.0 to 1.6, so neither recovery direction nor speed is the limiter there. Iteration 7 showed that cutting kd to 0.20 lost oval progress (0.3425 to 0.115), so kd stays at 0.30. Iteration 2 showed that the ±0.05 m spread removed oval line losses, which points to sensing span as the next lever.

Change: widen the sensor spread to x = -0.08, -0.04, 0, 0.04, 0.08 m. Weights stay at -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1. Every controller field stays at the iteration 6 values. This is one sensing change, as the Evaluator requested. Sensor_size 0.016 with 40 mm spacing leaves a 24 mm gap between footprints, which is slightly less than the 25 mm tape. So the tape always covers at least part of one sensor, though the signal may be weaker at the edges.

Expected result: s-bend and slalom line_loss_events drop toward 0, and their progress rises above about 0.16 and 0.11. Oval progress should stay near 0.34. Oval max_error may fall if the outer sensors catch the tape earlier. Hypotheses: (a) the wider array reduces s-bend and slalom line loss; (b) oval line loss stays at 0. If oval progress falls well below 0.34 or the score drops below 85.6, revert to the ±0.05 m spread and approve that design, since it is the best raced design. If the wider array changes nothing on s-bend and slalom, stop tuning those tracks and approve the best design.
